name: Battle rifleman, GER (our own design)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1.

helmets.name: plain
helmets.about: Issue M40 or M42 in rough matt field grey (the grit finish ordered March 1940), worn at the rim. The eagle decal on the left side is left off by the game's rule.

helmets.name: apple green, national shield
helmets.about: Smooth M35 in apple green with the black-white-red shield on the right side under the vent (ordered off on 21 March 1940; most helmets in Poland, fewer in France).

helmets.name: road dust
helmets.about: Plain helmet under a film of summer road dust (marches in the east).

helmets.name: band
helmets.about: A loop of inner tube (or a bread-bag strap) round the dome to hold foliage: often worn empty.

helmets.name: band and foliage
helmets.about: Inner-tube band with leafy twigs and grass pushed under it, densest at the front corners.

helmets.name: mud
helmets.about: Mud smeared on by hand to kill the shine (a soldier's habit all war).

helmets.name: net, scrim and foliage
helmets.about: The issue helmet net (from August 1942) or a cut-down vehicle net, with hessian strips and sprigs through it.

helmets.name: three-colour camouflage
helmets.about: Dark yellow sprayed over, with green and red-brown blotches in vehicle paint (paint ordered February 1943; most on helmets in Italy and Normandy).

helmets.name: wire and foliage
helmets.about: Chicken wire bent into a basket over a plain helmet and stuffed with hedge branches (the commonest Normandy look).

helmets.name: whitewash
helmets.about: Lime or white paint brushed over the field grey in winter, rubbed back to grey at the rim and high points (less common the first winter).

helmets.name: white cover
helmets.about: The white side of the issue snow cover, or a cut bedsheet tied round (from winter 1942).

helmets.name: desert tan
helmets.about: Tan sprayed at the depots over the field grey (ordered March 1941), bleached on top and chipped grey at the edges; mostly smooth.

helmets.name: sand, rough
helmets.about: The lighter sand (ordered March 1942), often with real sand in the paint.

about_variety: Variety (Tools/battle_units/variety.py and helmet_finishes.py): one man made into many. `faces` (8): face 0 is the man as he is; for face k, add `move` (metres, this file's axes) to the points listed in `at`, at each level of detail, then colour: every skin-painted point's colour times `tone`, and each point in `tint_at` times its `tint` (the hair, brows, stubble or moustache), all on top of the paint (and `shade`) as usual. `helmets`: his helmet (or cap, ushanka or hood) in the finishes it was worn in. Each is a rigid mesh at near/mid/far in the same form as the file's own meshes (points, facings, paints, triangles, part, part2, w2, and shade where the file has it), with `ink` at each point: -1 paints the point by its paint number as ever; any other value is an index into `inks` (colours, RRGGBB), the colour to paint it instead. To draw a man in a finish, leave out his own helmet's triangles, `helmet_tris[lod]` = [first, count] (they are the last of the list), and draw the finish's mesh skinned on the same bones. Each finish has `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM), `season` (any, summer, winter), `front` (any, east, west, south, desert, pacific, china) and `share` (how common it was). Picking, for each man: the finishes whose months hold the battle's date and whose season and front fit (any fits all), one chosen by share, and face = a hash of (block id, k) mod 8 and the helmet from another hash of the same, so a man keeps both all battle. When no finish fits the date, draw the first finish (or his own helmet). No swastika, rising-sun flag or fascist badge is drawn: the German eagle decal is left off (its side stays plain paint).
about_deaths: Deaths (Tools/battle_units/falls.py on ragdoll.py): every die_* clip named in `deaths` is a physics fall baked from this man's own body (his parts' masses, his joints' human ranges, the muscle tone going out of him, the ground under him; the rifle leaves his hand and lands where it lands), so no two kinds fall alike and none sinks into the ground. Pick: deaths[stance][kind], stance stand, run, kneel, prone or cover (what he was doing when hit), kind as the Fates picker's man_fall kinds (forward, back, side, knees, spin, thrown) or crawl (wounded: he falls, drags himself on a little, then goes still); one of the list by a hash of (block id, man). Play it once (loop false) and hold its last frame for the rest of the battle: the body stays where it fell. Each clip starts in the pose of `start` [clip, time] (blend into it over ~0.15 s from whatever he was doing); `end_offset` is where his pelvis ends (metres, his own axes; the clip is not in place: the pelvis and the rifle move); the weapon bone's last key is the rifle lying on the ground. Events: knee_down, body_fall, rifle_drop (and elbow_down in a crawl), at the time they touch. The older die_back, die_forward and die_kneel stay in the file as they were but are not in the table (they sink into the ground).
